newsitem.title: LATVIA: INTERBANK OVERNIGHT RATE FALLS SHARPLY.
newsitem.headline: INTERBANK OVERNIGHT RATE FALLS SHARPLY.

text.p: The overnight rate in Latvia's interbank market fell on Thursday to 1.5/2.0 percent from around 2.5 percent after an influx of lats caused by the purchase of a big chunk of Latvian Gas by German investors, dealers said.
German consortium Ruhrgas and Preussen bought 70 percent of its 16.25 percent stake in Latvian Gas for 7.8 million lats, the country's privatisation agency said on Thursday.
"There are suddenly a lot more lats on the market and that brought rates down," said one dealer.
"Another factor is the liquidity situation in the banks...it is common for rates to fall at the end of the month," the dealer added.
Interbank overnight rates were as high as 6.0 percent just one week ago, dealers said.
